repos.name: elementalsouls / Claude-BugHunter
repos.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 85 skills, 16 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerability classes, plus enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices.

summary.goal: claude-bughunter is a skill bundle for the Claude Code skills system, providing 85 skills and 16 slash commands for bug-bounty hunting and external red-team work. It covers 24 core vulnerability classes built from 681 disclosed HackerOne report patterns.
summary.usage: Install as a Claude Code plugin with `/plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter` followed by `/plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls`, or clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git and run `bash scripts/install.sh` (macOS/Linux) or the PowerShell equivalent. Skills then load automatically based on plain-English task descriptions.
summary.pros: The bundle includes enterprise identity and infrastructure attack matrices, engagement-folder scaffolding, and Burp MCP integration, with skills auto-triggered by topic rather than manual invocation. It also runs across multiple agent harnesses, including Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Hermes Agent, and Google AntiGravity.
summary.cons: The bundle explicitly excludes internal Active Directory attack techniques, C2 frameworks, post-exploitation/persistence tooling, and evasion methods, documenting these as deliberate scope exclusions rather than gaps, so separate tooling is needed for those engagement phases.
summary.fit: Given its documented scope and authorization language, the bundle appears best suited for researchers and red-team operators running authorized bug-bounty or external pentest engagements on assets they own or have written permission to test, rather than internal-network or post-compromise work.

repos.name: obra / superpowers
repos.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

summary.goal: Superpowers is presented as a complete software development methodology for coding agents, built on composable skills plus initial instructions that make sure the agent uses them.
summary.usage: Installation reportedly differs by coding-agent harness, and the README indicates separate installation is needed for each one in use. For Claude Code, the documented command is /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official via the official marketplace.
summary.pros: Skills appear to trigger automatically once installed, without extra invocation steps, and the workflow seems to enforce mandatory practices such as RED-GREEN-REFACTOR test-driven development and code review between tasks rather than treating them as optional suggestions.
summary.cons: A harness-specific install step suggests users running agents in multiple tools must repeat setup separately for each; the Hermes Agent section also notes it lacks a post-compaction hook, so a very long first session could reportedly lose the startup bootstrap.
summary.fit: This project seems best suited to users running coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, or similar supported harnesses who want an enforced, multi-stage development workflow rather than ad-hoc coding assistance.

repos.name: HKUDS / CLI-Anything
repos.description: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/

summary.goal: CLI-Anything is an open-source project (Apache 2.0) that converts software with an available codebase into agent-native command-line interfaces, so AI agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, and Pi can operate real applications through structured CLI commands instead of GUI automation.
summary.usage: Users can browse and install community-built CLIs with `pip install cli-anything-hub` followed by `cli-hub install <name>`, or generate a new CLI harness by adding the Claude Code marketplace (`/plugin marketplace add HKUDS/CLI-Anything`, `/plugin install cli-anything`) and running `/cli-anything ./gimp` to drive the 7-phase generator; Python 3.10+ is required.
summary.pros: The README reports 2,461 passing tests across the generated harnesses, Apache 2.0 licensing, and built-in JSON output for machine consumption alongside a human-readable REPL mode, with support spanning multiple agent platforms including Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Hermes, and Reasonix.
summary.cons: The documented Limitations section states that CLI-Anything relies on frontier-class models (e.g., Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4) for reliable generation, requires access to the target software's source code rather than compiled binaries, and often needs iterative `/refine` runs to reach production-quality coverage.
summary.fit: Based on the documented scope, the project appears best suited for teams or developers who want to expose existing open-source or internal software to AI agents without building custom APIs, though actual results may depend on the capability of the underlying agent model and the availability of source code.

repos.name: jingyaogong / minimind
repos.description: 🧠 两小时从 0 训出你的 64M 大模型。Train your own 64M LLM from scratch in 2 hours.

summary.goal: MiniMind's goal is to let individuals train a very small (~64M parameter) language model entirely from scratch, at an estimated cost of about 3 RMB and around 2 hours on a single NVIDIA 3090 GPU, covering pretraining, SFT, LoRA, RLHF/DPO, and RLAIF (PPO/GRPO/CISPO), Tool Use, and Agentic RL, implemented natively in PyTorch.
summary.usage: Clone the repository and install dependencies with `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/jingyaogong/minimind` and `pip install -r requirements.txt`; run inference via `python eval_llm.py --load_from ./minimind-3`, and run training stages such as `cd trainer && python train_pretrain.py` or `python train_full_sft.py`.
summary.pros: Core training algorithms (pretraining, SFT, LoRA, DPO, distillation) are implemented natively in PyTorch without relying on high-level third-party wrappers, while the project documents compatibility with transformers, trl, peft, and inference engines like llama.cpp, vllm, and ollama, plus multi-GPU DDP/DeepSpeed training with wandb/SwanLab logging.
summary.cons: The README's own benchmark results show weak English-language performance because training data is weighted toward Chinese, and the custom tokenizer's vocabulary is limited to 6,400 tokens, notably smaller than tokenizers used by comparable open models.
summary.fit: This appears best suited to learners and researchers wanting a hands-on, reproducible path through full LLM training pipelines on a single consumer GPU, rather than to those seeking a production-ready model with strong multilingual or large-scale capability.

repos.name: cursor / plugins
repos.description: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins

summary.goal: This repository, cursor/plugins, hosts official Cursor plugins for popular developer tools, frameworks, and SaaS products. Each plugin lives in its own directory with a .cursor-plugin/plugin.json manifest.
summary.usage: The repository is structured as a multi-plugin marketplace: a root .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json file lists all plugins, and each plugin folder has its own .cursor-plugin/plugin.json manifest, along with skills/, rules/, an mcp.json file for MCP server definitions, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, and LICENSE. No explicit installation command is documented, so usage presumably involves Cursor loading plugins through this marketplace structure.
summary.pros: The catalog lists more than 100 plugins across categories such as Developer Tools, Productivity, Integrations, and Finance and Legal, covering tools like GitHub, Salesforce, Google Workspace apps, PayPal, and QuickBooks. For example, the Easyship plugin compares courier rates across 550+ couriers.
summary.cons: Some integrations are explicitly marked Beta, such as Salesforce (Headless 360, Beta), suggesting reduced stability for those plugins. The README does not document explicit installation or setup commands, so configuring a plugin for use may require steps not spelled out in this document.
summary.fit: This repository appears suited for teams or individuals using Cursor who want ready-made integrations with many SaaS and developer tools, rather than needing to build custom connectors themselves.

repos.name: firecrawl / firecrawl
repos.description: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and access 550+ data providers through one API.

summary.goal: Firecrawl is knowledge infrastructure intended to make AI agents smarter by turning websites into clean markdown and structured data. The README describes three ways to use it: Firecrawl Local (a self-hosted binary), Firecrawl Cloud (a hosted service), and full self-hosting of the server from this repository.
summary.usage: Firecrawl Local installs via `cargo install firecrawl-local` (requires Rust and a C compiler), and commands like `firecrawl-local scrape`, `firecrawl-local crawl`, and `firecrawl-local serve` handle scraping, crawling, and running a local API on port 3002. The Python and Node SDKs install with `pip install firecrawl` and `npm install firecrawl`.
summary.pros: The README states Firecrawl Cloud covers 96% of the web including JS-heavy pages, with a P95 latency of 3.4 seconds, and returns LLM-ready markdown, structured JSON, and screenshots. Firecrawl Keyless offers 1,000 free credits a month without an API key or signup.
summary.cons: Running Firecrawl Local requires installing Rust and a C compiler toolchain (e.g., Xcode command line tools or build-essential), an extra setup step compared to using the hosted Cloud service. The core server is also licensed under AGPL-3.0, a copyleft license that may impose obligations in some deployment scenarios, though SDKs are MIT licensed.
summary.fit: This project appears suited for teams building AI agents that need web data, offering options from a single local binary to a fully self-hosted server with Docker Compose, Redis, PostgreSQL, and a browser service. Self-hosting likely requires more operational effort than using Firecrawl Cloud directly.

repos.name: nginx / nginx
repos.description: The official NGINX Open Source repository.

summary.goal: NGINX is described as a widely used web server that also functions as a high performance load balancer, reverse proxy, API gateway, and content cache. It is free and open source software distributed under a simplified 2-clause BSD-like license.
summary.usage: The README documents cloning the source with `git clone https://github.com/nginx/nginx.git`, then running `auto/configure` followed by `make` to build, and `sudo make install` to install the binary (installed into `/usr/local/nginx/`). The compiled binary can be run with `sudo /usr/local/nginx/sbin/nginx`, and operation can be verified with `curl localhost`.
summary.pros: Binary packages are available for all major operating systems and Linux distributions, and official package repositories ensure the most recent release, features, fixes, and security patches. Dynamic modules, such as NGINX JavaScript (njs), can be installed after the core binaries are built without recompiling, and worker processes can auto-scale to available CPU cores.
summary.cons: Building from source requires installing dependency libraries such as `libpcre3-dev` and `zlib1g-dev` beforehand (with additional libraries like `libssl-dev` needed for SSL support), which suggests the build process has prerequisites that must be satisfied before compilation succeeds. The README also notes that the Windows implementation is at the Proof-of-Concept stage and is intended only for development and testing, not production use.
summary.fit: This project appears suited for users needing a web server, reverse proxy, load balancer, or API gateway on Linux, FreeBSD, or similar Unix-like systems, with precompiled packages simplifying deployment. Given the Proof-of-Concept status noted for Windows, it may be less suited for production Windows deployments.

repos.name: openvinotoolkit / openvino
repos.description: OpenVINO™ is an open source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference

summary.goal: OpenVINO (openvinotoolkit/openvino) is documented as an open-source software toolkit for optimizing and deploying deep learning models, aimed at inference optimization for computer vision, automatic speech recognition, generative AI, and natural language processing tasks.
summary.usage: The README documents installing via `pip install -U openvino`, and verifying the install by running `import openvino as ov; print(ov.__version__)` in Python.
summary.pros: Documented strengths include broad platform compatibility (CPU x86/ARM, GPU, and Intel NPU accelerators), support for models from PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, Keras, PaddlePaddle, and JAX/Flax, and an ecosystem of integrations such as NNCF, Optimum Intel, LangChain, and LlamaIndex.
summary.cons: The README states that OpenVINO collects software performance and usage data by default (directly or via Google Analytics 4), so users must explicitly run `opt_in_out --opt_out` if they want to disable this telemetry.
summary.fit: Given its documented device and framework support, OpenVINO appears best suited for teams deploying inference workloads across CPU, GPU, and NPU hardware for vision, speech, or generative AI tasks, though the README recommends checking system requirements and supported devices before setup.

repos.name: cathrynlavery / diagram-design
repos.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid, Qoder, and Pi. 52 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.

summary.goal: Diagram Design is an agent skill that generates diagrams as a single self-contained HTML + SVG file matching a defined brand style, covering 52 diagram types such as architecture, sequence, and flowchart diagrams.
summary.usage: Install with `npx skills add cathrynlavery/diagram-design`, or in Claude Code run `/plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagram-design` followed by `/plugin install diagram-design@diagram-design`. Diagrams are produced by asking the connected agent for one in plain language, and the bundled gallery (`skills/diagram-design/assets/index.html`) can be opened locally to preview the diagram types.
summary.pros: Output is a single HTML file with no build step, JavaScript, or external image dependency, templates include accessibility features such as ARIA labeling and automatic WCAG contrast checks, and a brand-onboarding flow extracts colors and fonts from a website while reporting results in a fidelity receipt.
summary.cons: The README notes that output quality depends on the model running it and that the same prompt can lay out differently between runs, and that the generated diagram is not an editable source format, so there is no text to diff in a pull request or canvas to adjust directly.
summary.fit: The README positions this skill for diagrams meant to be published rather than iterated on in version control; for diagrams that live in Git and change every sprint, it states Mermaid is still the better fit.

repos.name: mvanhorn / last30days-skill
repos.description: AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web - then synthesizes a grounded summary

summary.goal: last30days is a Claude Code skill (and a package usable on other Agent Skills hosts) that runs an AI-agent-led search across platforms such as Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, Polymarket, and GitHub, scoring results by upvotes, likes, and real-money signals rather than editorial curation, then synthesizing them into a single research brief.
summary.usage: Install in Claude Code with `/plugin marketplace add mvanhorn/last30days-skill` followed by `/plugin install last30days`, or on other supported hosts (Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, and 50+ others) with `npx skills add mvanhorn/last30days-skill -g`. Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket, and GitHub work with zero configuration; running it once triggers a setup wizard that can unlock sources like X, YouTube, and TikTok.
summary.pros: The skill searches many platforms in parallel and ranks findings by real engagement — upvotes, likes, view counts, and market odds backed by real money — rather than SEO or editorial placement, aiming to surface what communities are actually discussing within a recent 30-day window.
summary.cons: Several sources beyond the zero-config set (Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub) require API keys, browser authentication, or explicit opt-in flags, so full source coverage depends on added credentials and setup. Claude Desktop installs also keep a credential store separate from the Code skill, so keys must be re-entered there, and Windows support for the Claude Desktop extension is currently deferred.
summary.fit: Given its design around bringing your own API keys and browser sessions to bridge otherwise separate platforms, the tool seems best suited for users who want consolidated, engagement-ranked research across many Agent-Skills-compatible hosts rather than a single dedicated search interface.

repos.name: google-labs-code / stitch-skills
repos.description: A library of Agent Skills designed to work with the Stitch MCP server. Each skill follows the Agent Skills open standard, for compatibility with coding agents such as Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor.

summary.goal: stitch-skills is a repository of agent skills and plugins for Google Stitch, following the Agent Skills open standard. It is documented as compatible with coding agents including Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode (manual install).
summary.usage: For Codex, run `codex plugin marketplace add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --ref main` (optionally with --sparse paths) to add the marketplace. For Claude Code, run `npx plugins add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --scope project --target claude-code`. To install individual skills, run `npx skills add google-labs-code/stitch-skills`.
summary.pros: The repository separates functionality into three plugins (stitch-design, stitch-build, stitch-utilities), letting users install only the skills they need, and supports sparse checkouts to speed up installation.
summary.cons: Skills require a separately configured Stitch MCP server with its own credentials and environment variables before they can run, and selectively installed skills may need manually resolved inter-dependencies.
summary.fit: This appears best suited for teams already using Google Stitch alongside a supported coding agent; OpenCode users should note it needs manual skill and MCP setup rather than the marketplace flow used by Codex or Claude Code.

repos.name: mjmirza / app-store-compliance
repos.description: Avoid common App Store and Google Play rejections. Open playbook and pre-submission guard with 125 documented rejection patterns and fixes, privacy manifest and Data safety checks, 117 tracked deadlines (EU AI Act, DSA, COPPA, age laws), and a skill for AI coding agents.

summary.goal: App Store Compliance Playbook is a documentation and scripting project for mjmirza/app-store-compliance that aims to catch Apple App Store and Google Play rejection causes before a human reviewer does. It positions itself as a reference plus pre-submission guard for iOS and Android apps, and the README states explicitly that it does not guarantee approval.
summary.usage: Usage starts with two commands: `git clone https://github.com/mjmirza/app-store-compliance ~/repositories/app-store-compliance` followed by running the bundled `app-store-compliance-guard.sh` script with the path to the app's project folder. For continuous use inside AI coding tools such as Claude Code, the README describes `bash ~/repositories/app-store-compliance/scripts/install.sh --tool all` to wire the guard into the tool's submit workflow.
summary.pros: The README lists catching rejection risks before App Store or Google Play review, mapping each rejection pattern to a specific guideline and fix, prioritizing the two most common causes (a working demo account and an accurate privacy declaration), and supporting both developers and non-developers through a plain-language checklist.
summary.cons: A 'CLEAR' scan result is explicitly not an approval, since account and listing checks still require manual review; the README also notes that the rule set is flagged 'STALE' after 60 days and needs a `git pull` update.
summary.fit: Licensing terms (OpenRoots Agent License 2.3) make it free for individuals and organizations with revenue at or below USD 20 million, suggesting it is primarily aimed at individual developers, small teams, and smaller companies rather than larger enterprises, which would owe a capped royalty above that threshold.

repos.name: Tracer-Cloud / opensre
repos.description: The open-source agent for CI/CD reliability.

summary.goal: OpenSRE is an open-source CLI agent built to investigate CI/CD pipeline failures: it reads a failed run's logs, traces the root cause, and pushes a fix for review. It is described as self-hosted and designed to work with your own LLM models.
summary.usage: Install it on macOS or Linux with `curl -fsSL https://install.opensre.com | bash -s -- -gh`, or the PowerShell equivalent on Windows, then launch the interactive shell with `opensre`. For one-off, non-interactive runs (e.g. in a CI script), use `opensre ask "why is checkout-api slow?"`.
summary.pros: The agent separates CI-caused failures from code-caused ones and gives evidence-linked answers rather than just a failure notice. It also connects to 60+ integrations spanning LLM providers, observability platforms (Grafana, Datadog, CloudWatch), infrastructure (Kubernetes, AWS), and incident tools (Slack, PagerDuty, GitHub).
summary.cons: The project carries a public-alpha status, so core workflows are described as usable but not yet fully stable, and APIs/integrations may still change. Self-hosted deployment also appears to require configuring your own LLM_PROVIDER and API key rather than a turnkey managed service.
summary.fit: Given its self-hosted, bring-your-own-model design and CI/CD/incident-response focus, OpenSRE seems best suited to engineering teams already running CI pipelines and observability stacks who want an agent they control, rather than teams seeking a fully managed, zero-setup SaaS tool.

repos.name: toeverything / AFFiNE
repos.description: There can be more than Notion and Miro. AFFiNE(pronounced [ə‘fain]) is a next-gen knowledge base that brings planning, sorting and creating all together. Privacy first, open-source, customizable and ready to use.

summary.goal: AFFiNE is described in its README as an open-source, all-in-one workspace that merges documents, whiteboard canvas, and databases into a single platform, positioned as an alternative to Notion and Miro. It emphasizes local-first data ownership and real-time collaboration.
summary.usage: The README describes several ways to run AFFiNE: self-hosting via Docker (with one-click deploy options for Render and Sealos), building from source following BUILDING.md, or opening a GitHub Codespace via the 'Code' button and selecting 'Create codespace on master'. A hosted live demo is also linked at app.affine.pro.
summary.pros: AFFiNE combines rich-text docs, sticky notes, embedded pages, and multi-view databases on one edgeless canvas, supports real-time sync across platforms, and its Community Edition is free and open-source under the MIT license.
summary.cons: The README states that the Enterprise Edition (EE), which would add features like SSO and advanced admin/audit tools, is 'yet to be published,' so organizations needing those capabilities cannot use them yet. Contributing code also requires signing a Contributor License Agreement before any pull request can be merged.
summary.fit: Based on the described features, AFFiNE appears best suited to individuals or teams wanting a self-hosted, privacy-oriented workspace that merges note-taking with visual canvas tools; it may be less immediately fitting for organizations specifically requiring the not-yet-released enterprise SSO/admin features.

repos.name: XiaoYouChR / Ghost-Downloader-3
repos.description: The only downloader you need. 下载器的集大成者。

summary.goal: Ghost Downloader 3 is a desktop and mobile download manager that aims to consolidate multiple protocols—HTTP, Magnet/BT, FTP, M3U8, MPEG-DASH, and eD2k—plus site-specific downloading from YouTube, Bilibili, GitHub, and HuggingFace into a single application for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
summary.usage: After installing the app, the `ghd` command-line tool can be installed from Settings -> Command Line Tool. Core commands include `ghd probe <url>` to preview a URL without starting a task, `ghd add <url>...` to add and start download tasks, and `ghd wait <taskId>` to wait for a task to finish.
summary.pros: The README describes smart chunking without file merging, automatic bandwidth detection, and real-browser TLS fingerprints intended to avoid anti-bot blocking. It also offers an aria2-compatible RPC API for third-party tool integration, a browser extension for sniffing downloadable media, and native builds across all four supported platforms.
summary.cons: Documentation notes that Qt 6.6+ no longer supports CPUs lacking the AVX instruction set, which may limit use on older hardware. Minimum OS versions are also required (Windows 10+, macOS 13.0+, glibc 2.35+ on Linux, Android 9.0+), and the plugin API is still listed as an open roadmap item rather than finalized, so third-party Feature Packs support may not yet be fully stable.
summary.fit: The project appears best suited to users who want one tool covering many download protocols and sites rather than separate apps, and who are on reasonably current operating systems meeting the listed version minimums. It is distributed under the GPL v3.0 license.

repos.name: zhouxiaoka / autoclip
repos.description: AutoClip｜The open-source OpusClip alternative — local-first AI clipping & MCP server, zero subscriptions. 一个链接，一键出片。开源 AI 视频剪辑桌面工具，将播客、访谈、课程等长视频自动剪成短视频，生成字幕、封面和发布文案，适配抖音、小红书、TikTok、Reels 与 YouTube Shorts。

summary.goal: AutoClip is an open-source, local-first application that turns videos, links, or live stream replays into ready-to-post short clips, offering smart reframing, captions, covers, and titles, with built-in MCP support for AI agents.
summary.usage: Install via desktop app (.dmg/.exe from GitHub Releases), or run `uvx autoclip-mcp` for CLI/MCP use, or `docker compose up -d --build` for self-hosted setup; outputs can be produced with commands like `autoclip produce talk.mp4 --srt talk.srt --platform tiktok`.
summary.pros: It is free and MIT-licensed with no subscriptions, since cutting and rendering run locally; it supports offline operation via Ollama/LM Studio with Whisper/SenseVoice, and offers 6 live replay sources (OBS, Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Discord, local recordings) plus 13 languages in the UI.
summary.cons: Cloud analysis, transcription, and AI covers require the user's own API keys at provider rates, and unsigned desktop builds may require manual steps such as removing macOS quarantine attributes or bypassing Windows SmartScreen, suggesting code-signing/notarization is still in progress.
summary.fit: This tool seems best suited for creators of podcasts, interviews, and gaming streams who want local, subscription-free clip generation, and for developers integrating AI agents via MCP/CLI, though cloud-dependent features still rely on third-party provider costs.

repos.name: backnotprop / plannotator
repos.description: The workspace to stay in the loop and on top of agents - shape, decide, plan, annotate, review code, share with team, and send all feedback to agents with one click.

summary.goal: Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, Pi) and personal assistants, letting users annotate plans, specs, markdown, HTML artifacts, and diffs/PRs and send feedback back to the agent.
summary.usage: Install with `curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash` on macOS/Linux/WSL or `irm https://plannotator.ai/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows PowerShell; then use commands like `/plannotator-review` to review a diff or `/plannotator-annotate <file>` to annotate a document, with `plannotator inbox` opening the Plannotator Inbox window.
summary.pros: It plugs into agents via plugins, hooks, and slash commands so review feedback flows directly back into the active agent session; it supports version control systems including Git, GitButler, Jujutsu, Perforce, GitHub, and GitLab, and offers guided reviews that split diffs into chapters.
summary.cons: The installer may contact GitHub and npm for release resolution, agent files, and extras like Pi, so a full install likely requires network access beyond the download itself, though pinning `--version` only skips GitHub API release resolution, not the download.
summary.fit: Plannotator appears suited for developers who want a local review layer across multiple coding agents and version control backends; teams wanting shared review appear to need the separate Workspaces feature, currently only available via a waitlist.

repos.name: GoogleChrome / modern-web-guidance-src
repos.description: Keep your coding agent up to date with the latest web best practices

summary.goal: Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embeds web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into coding agents' context, maintained by the GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src source repository. It aims to steer coding agents away from legacy JavaScript patterns toward modern, native web platform APIs for performance, accessibility, and UI needs.
summary.usage: Install the skill interactively with `npx modern-web-guidance@latest install` (requires Node.js 22 or later), or try it without installing using commands such as `npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop"`, `npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer"`, and `npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan .` to scan a codebase for legacy patterns.
summary.pros: The project documents coverage of 269 modern web features and 206 real-world developer use cases spanning CSS, HTML/DOM, JavaScript APIs, accessibility, performance, security, and more. Published eval snapshots report measurable uplift when agents use the guidance versus unguided baselines, for example reported gains of roughly +35 to +41 percentage points across several agent/model combinations on recent dates.
summary.cons: Using the primary installer requires Node.js 22 or later, which may limit use in older environments. The CLI also sends anonymous usage telemetry (installation counts, retrieval IDs, and search queries) by default when online, requiring an explicit `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` environment variable to opt out; this telemetry behavior could be an operational consideration for privacy-sensitive setups.
summary.fit: Modern Web Guidance appears best suited for teams integrating AI coding agents into web development workflows who want guidance toward native browser APIs rather than legacy JavaScript libraries or heavy polyfills. Organizations with Node.js version constraints, telemetry restrictions, or agents outside the documented installation methods (npx, Vercel Skills CLI, GitHub CLI, various plugin marketplaces) may need to verify compatibility before adoption.

repos.name: n8n-io / nod
repos.description: Open source personal agent with its own computer. It chases invoices, preps your calls and cancels trials on real websites, and asks before it acts. Runs on your machine with the model you choose. By n8n.

summary.goal: Nod is an open source personal AI agent that runs on the user's own machine, performing real tasks such as invoice follow-ups, meeting preparation, and cancelling subscriptions on actual websites and apps like Gmail, Calendar, Slack, and Notion, asking for approval before acting on the user's behalf.
summary.usage: Nod can be installed via prebuilt binaries for macOS or Windows, or run from source: on macOS or Linux, install Node.js 24.21+, pnpm, and Docker, then run `git clone https://github.com/n8n-io/nod.git`, `cd nod`, `corepack enable`, and `pnpm start`. After setup (about ten minutes), users connect a model provider and apps, then issue requests via the app, Telegram, or WhatsApp.
summary.pros: It supports many model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure, and others) or ChatGPT Plus/Pro sign-in, keeps files, memory, and saved logins local, requires approval for risky actions, and reports a 98% task completion rate and 93.2% memory recall in internal benchmarks.
summary.cons: Nod is labeled a research preview, so it may make mistakes since its safety check relies on model judgment; it likely requires the host computer or server to remain on for scheduled tasks, since the README states schedules do not run when the machine is off and a hosted version is not yet available.
summary.fit: Nod seems best suited for individuals or teams wanting a locally run, approval-gated personal assistant for routine web and app chores, though Windows and Linux support are still in preview and continuous operation likely requires dedicated hardware like a Mac mini or self-hosted server.

repos.name: alibaba / open-code-review
repos.description: Secure, fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.

summary.goal: Open Code Review (OCR) is an AI-powered code review CLI tool that originated as Alibaba Group's internal code review assistant before being open-sourced. It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM via an agent with tool-use capabilities, and generates structured, line-level review comments; `ocr scan` can also review entire files without a diff.
summary.usage: Install globally with `npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review`, then configure a provider with `ocr config provider` and `ocr config model` before running `ocr review` (or `ocr scan` for full-file review). Agent Skills can also be added via `npx skills add alibaba/open-code-review` for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Kimi Code.
summary.pros: According to the README's benchmark, compared to general-purpose agents (Claude Code) on the same underlying model, Open Code Review achieves higher Precision and F1 while consuming only about 1/9 of the tokens and completing reviews faster, based on a benchmark of 50 repositories, 200 pull requests, and 1,505 annotated issues.
summary.cons: The documented Recall is lower than general-purpose agents, described as a deliberate trade-off favoring precision over noise; native mode also requires Git >= 2.41 and a separately configured LLM provider, which may involve authentication and cost considerations.
summary.fit: It appears suited for teams wanting deterministic, line-precise code review integrated into Git workflows or CI/CD pipelines, particularly where token cost and review stability matter more than maximal defect recall.

repos.name: ChromeDevTools / chrome-devtools-mcp
repos.description: Chrome DevTools for coding agents

summary.goal: chrome-devtools-mcp (Chrome DevTools for agents) is a Model-Context-Protocol server and CLI that lets coding agents such as Claude, Cursor, or Copilot control and inspect a live Chrome browser for automation, debugging, and performance analysis.
summary.usage: Configure an MCP client with the command `npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest`, or install the CLI globally with `npm i chrome-devtools-mcp@latest -g` and run commands such as `chrome-devtools navigate_page 1 --url "https://developers.chrome.com"`.
summary.pros: It records performance traces with actionable insights, supports network, screenshot, and console debugging with source-mapped stack traces, and automates browser actions reliably through puppeteer, which waits for action results automatically.
summary.cons: chrome-devtools-mcp exposes browser content to MCP clients, so sensitive or personal data should not be shared during sessions; official support covers only Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing; and usage statistics collection is enabled by default, requiring the `--no-usage-statistics` flag to opt out.
summary.fit: This tool likely suits teams already using MCP-compatible coding agents who can maintain a Node.js LTS runtime, npm, and a current stable Chrome installation for development and debugging workflows.

repos.name: tradermonty / claude-trading-skills
repos.description: Claude Code skills for equity investors and traders — market analysis, technical charting, economic calendars, screeners, and trading strategy development.

summary.goal: Claude Trading Skills is a Claude Skills-based trading workflow toolkit for time-constrained individual investors who use long-term investing, ETFs, and dividend stocks as a core strategy, with disciplined swing trading as a satellite when conditions allow. It structures market review, risk management, trade planning, journaling, and continuous improvement rather than outsourcing buy/sell decisions to AI; it is explicitly not a signal service or a promise of profitability.
summary.usage: Clone the repository and, for Claude Code, copy a skill folder (e.g. backtest-expert) to ~/.claude/skills/ or .claude/skills/ inside a project. For the Claude web app, download a .skill package from the latest GitHub Release and upload it under Customize > Skills. Developers can rebuild a package with `python3 scripts/package_skills.py --skill <skill-name>`.
summary.pros: A documented no-API-key starter path (market-breadth-analyzer, uptrend-analyzer, position-sizer, trader-memory-core, signal-postmortem) lets users review markets, size trades, journal decisions, and review outcomes using public CSVs and local files, without paid data subscriptions. The repository also provides a broad catalog of skills across market regime, portfolio, dividend, swing, and strategy-research areas, each tracked in a canonical skills-index.yaml.
summary.cons: Several higher-value skills (e.g. portfolio-manager, FMP/FINVIZ-based screeners) require optional or required paid integrations such as Alpaca, FMP, or FINVIZ Elite, with FINVIZ Elite costing $39.50/month or $299.50/year; the README also notes "no API" does not mean "no external data," since even starter-path skills still need public CSVs, chart screenshots, or local files.
summary.fit: This toolkit fits individual investors wanting a structured, human-reviewed decision process rather than automated execution; the README states it is not designed for fully automated trading, signal outsourcing, or short-term scalping, and all trading decisions remain the user's responsibility under an MIT License provided "AS IS, WITHOUT WARRANTY."

repos.name: ag-ui-protocol / ag-ui
repos.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.

summary.goal: AG-UI is described as an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications, replacing custom per-framework wiring with one bi-directional event stream so agents can power web, mobile, terminal, or Slack clients.
summary.usage: A new app can be scaffolded with `npx create-ag-ui-app@latest`, or developers can speak the protocol directly by installing `pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn` for a Python agent server and `npm install @ag-ui/client tsx` for a TypeScript client, per the documented quick-start example.
summary.pros: The README states AG-UI 1.0 has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema with TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs generated from it, is backwards compatible between 0.x and 1.0, and is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle with integrations across many agent frameworks.
summary.cons: The Python agent quick-start requires Python 3.9+ and the TypeScript client requires Node.js 20+, and the generated CopilotKit templates call OpenAI, requiring an `OPENAI_API_KEY` to be set before running.
summary.fit: AG-UI is positioned as complementary to MCP (tools/context) and A2A (agent-to-agent), serving specifically the agent-to-user connection layer, suggesting it fits projects needing a framework-agnostic transport for streaming chat, shared state, or human-in-the-loop UI rather than tool-calling or inter-agent communication alone.

repos.name: meta / astryx
repos.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready

summary.goal: Astryx is an open source design system, currently in Beta, built on React 19+ and StyleX. It is presented as having grown inside Meta over eight years into the company's most-used design system, powering 13,000+ apps, and appears intended to let both people and AI assistants build UI the same way, though this framing is the project's own description.
summary.usage: Install the core package, a theme, and StyleX with `npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex` (plus `npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli`), then run `npx @astryxdesign/cli init` once to complete setup; this prints getting-started steps and saves a guide to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.
summary.pros: It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, and templates as one system. Components allow 'swizzling' to eject full source for ownership, and styling can be overridden via `className` with Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS instead of adopting StyleX directly.
summary.cons: React 19 or later is a required peer dependency, which may limit use in projects on earlier React versions. The project is marked Beta, and packages such as @astryxdesign/lab, @astryxdesign/vega, and @astryxdesign/charts are either unpublished or available only under the @canary tag with no stable release yet, suggesting some areas of the system are still maturing.
summary.fit: This seems best suited for teams adopting a full design system with CLI-driven workflows who want shared, documented conventions usable by both developers and AI coding assistants. It may be less suitable for projects requiring React below version 19 or stable chart/visualization components, since those remain canary-only.

repos.name: pookjw / HermesEnabler
repos.description: Enable Hermès Watch Faces on any Apple Watch devices

summary.goal: HermesEnabler2 appears to be a tool for installing a developer-mode-related enabler app onto a paired Apple Watch; the README states it is supported on watchOS 27.0 through 27.3 beta 1.
summary.usage: On macOS, download the IPA from GitHub Releases and sideload it with Sideloadly, or build and run HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj directly in Xcode; after installing, open HermesEnabler2 on the Watch and follow its in-app steps. On Windows, download watchbridge-windows.zip from WatchBridge Releases, extract it, and run WatchBridge.exe to prepare Developer Mode and install the same IPA.
summary.pros: Two independent installation paths are documented — sideloading or Xcode on macOS, and the separate WatchBridge tool on Windows — and once the iPhone and Watch are paired over USB, subsequent installs and renewals can proceed over Wi-Fi.
summary.cons: The README states watchOS 26 is not supported, limiting compatibility to watchOS 27.0 through 27.3 beta 1; it also notes WatchBridge is an unsigned, community-maintained tool unaffiliated with Apple or this project, and that it supports only one paired Watch at a time.
summary.fit: This seems intended for users with an Apple Watch on one of the specific supported watchOS versions who are willing to sideload unsigned software; the README explicitly states use is at the user's own risk.

repos.name: we-promise / sure
repos.description: The personal finance app for everyone (by everyone)

summary.goal: Sure is a personal finance application and community-maintained fork of the discontinued Maybe Finance project, offering self-hosted tracking of cashflow, net worth, and spending.
summary.usage: Sure can be self-hosted via Docker or run locally for development: run `cp .env.local.example .env.local`, `bin/setup`, and `bin/dev`, then visit http://localhost:3000; optional demo data can be loaded with `rake demo_data:default`.
summary.pros: It supports access from a browser, macOS desktop app, mobile app, API clients, and LLM agents, and offers multiple one-click deployment options including Render, PikaPods, and Hostim, all under the AGPLv3 open-source license.
summary.cons: Local development requires specific prerequisites — a Ruby version matching `.ruby-version`, PostgreSQL newer than 9.3, and Redis newer than 5.4 — and the project maintains a public dashboard tracking known performance issues on data-heavy requests.
summary.fit: Given its AGPLv3 licensing and the explicit restriction against using the "Maybe" trademark in forks, Sure likely suits individuals or communities wanting a self-hosted, community-driven personal finance tool rather than an officially branded product.

repos.name: obsidianmd / obsidian-skills
repos.description: Teach your agent to use Obsidian and open formats including Markdown, Bases, JSON Canvas.

summary.goal: obsidian-skills provides a set of Agent Skills for use with Obsidian. These skills follow the Agent Skills specification, so they can be used with agents such as Claude Code, Claude, ChatGPT, Antigravity, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Grok Bot, Hermes Agent, Kiro, Muse, and OpenCode.
summary.usage: For Claude Code, install with `claude plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills` followed by `claude plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills`. Other agents can instead install directly from the repository using `npx skills add https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills`, which prompts for which agent to install into.
summary.pros: The repository bundles several distinct skills: obsidian-markdown for Obsidian Flavored Markdown, obsidian-bases for Obsidian Bases files, json-canvas for JSON Canvas files, obsidian-cli for vault interaction via the Obsidian CLI, obsidian-headless for syncing and publishing without the desktop app, defuddle for extracting clean markdown from web pages, and knap for rendering Markdown templates from JSON or CSV data.
summary.cons: When used through Muse, which runs in Meta's cloud, the obsidian-cli skill does not work, so vault access there is limited to functionality compatible with that cloud environment.
summary.fit: Given the range of supported agents and skills covering markdown editing, vault syncing, and templating, the project appears best suited to users who manage Obsidian vaults through AI agents and want consistent skill behavior across desktop, CLI, and cloud-hosted clients, though compatibility may vary somewhat by agent, as with the noted Muse limitation.

repos.name: dream-num / univer
repos.description: Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK. Bring editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing into your product for people and AI agents. Built on an extensible open-source core.

summary.goal: Univer is an Office SDK for embedding Office editing capabilities—spreadsheets, documents, slides, canvases, and PDFs (including Sheets and Docs)—into a developer's own application. It provides editing, calculation, collaboration, and file-processing building blocks for people and agents, using the application's own data and permissions.
summary.usage: Install with `pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core` in a Vite-based browser project, add a container element, call `createUniver` with the Sheets Core preset, then run `univerAPI.createWorkbook({})` to render an editable spreadsheet.
summary.pros: The repository's open-source Web SDK core—content models, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets/Docs editing—is licensed under Apache-2.0 and reusable in commercial applications. Features split into content-logic and UI plugins with explicit dependency declarations, giving custom features clear boundaries and consistent extension points.
summary.cons: Older or non-standard environments may need a polyfill for `Intl.Segmenter`; developing the monorepo itself requires Node.js >=22.18, while Headless usage needs Node.js >=18.17.0, suggesting some runtime setup may be required depending on target environment. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and AI SDK extensions are licensed separately, and freemium evaluation includes watermarks and feature limits.
summary.fit: Univer appears suited to teams building browser-based Office editing features with bundlers like Vite, esbuild, or Webpack 5, targeting Chrome >=88, Edge >=90, Firefox >=88, Safari >=14.1, or Electron >=12, with a React 18/19 view layer (minimal support for React 16.9+/17).

repos.name: kajisho5 / ffmpeg-skill
repos.description: Local video editor for coding agents: 42 FFmpeg tools with a machine-readable contract and an MCP server, for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Cut, captions, reframe, loudness, platform exports. No cloud, no API keys.

summary.goal: ffmpeg-skill is an Agent Skill that gives coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor and Codex (or any MCP client) a local FFmpeg-based video and audio editor. It teaches a probe → edit → check → verify workflow and ships 42 tools performing the actual FFmpeg/ffprobe operations, entirely offline with no API keys.
summary.usage: Install with `npx ffmpeg-skill setup` (or `npx ffmpeg-skill` for a single agent), which installs the skill, installs FFmpeg if missing, and finishes with `doctor`. Run `npx ffmpeg-skill doctor` afterward to confirm required FFmpeg components and `npx ffmpeg-skill contract --json` to inspect the tool contract.
summary.pros: The README describes 42 standalone Python tools (cut, join, silence removal, captions, color grading, loudness normalization, delivery checks, and more), each independently verifiable through probing and visual contact sheets. A machine-readable contract is generated directly from each tool's argparse parser, which the project states keeps CLI, documentation, and the MCP schema from drifting out of sync. Processing runs locally, so footage is not uploaded.
summary.cons: Using it requires `ffmpeg` and `python3` already available on PATH, and the plain Homebrew `ffmpeg` formula is documented as lacking filters such as subtitles and zscale, requiring `ffmpeg-full` instead. Optional speech-to-text captioning needs a separately installed engine (e.g., faster-whisper) that downloads a model on first run. Only 12 of the 42 tools carry a "stable" compatibility guarantee; the other 30 are documented as "beta" and may still change.
summary.fit: This appears suited to users running AI coding agents who want local, scriptable FFmpeg editing without cloud services or API keys. The README positions this repo as the execution "hands" within a wider kajisho5 video-production ecosystem, with separate repos handling editorial decisions or typed editing graphs.

repos.name: Nutlope / hallmark
repos.description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

summary.goal: Hallmark is a design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode, made by Together AI and documented at https://www.usehallmark.com. It aims to generate web pages that avoid common visual tells associated with AI-generated design, applying a baseline of checks before building a page.
summary.usage: Install with `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g`. Invoked harnesses can run commands such as `/hallmark redesign <path>` or `/hallmark audit <path>`, or a described build request, depending on the tool.
summary.pros: The project offers fifty selectable themes plus a custom design mode, dedicated redesign and audit commands, 755 openly licensed credited photographs, and an automated lint pass (sloplint) checking pages against known AI-style design tells.
summary.cons: The tool requires Node 18 or later, and its browser-based checks (such as rendering and screenshots) need an additional global install of puppeteer-core plus Chrome; without these, only static checks run.
summary.fit: Hallmark appears best suited to teams already using Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, or OpenCode, since it integrates as a skill or plugin within those harnesses rather than as a standalone application.

repos.name: cloudflare / security-audit-skill
repos.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings

summary.goal: security-audit is a skill that turns a coding agent into a security auditor, running audits through six phases: reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting. It is the single-repo starting point from which Cloudflare's multi-stage vulnerability discovery harness evolved.
summary.usage: Install via the Skills CLI with `npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill --skill security-audit` (add `--global` for a user-level install). Inside the codebase to audit, ask the coding agent to run a request such as `security audit this codebase`; an unspecified output directory defaults to `~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N>`.
summary.pros: The workflow uses adversarial validation, where the agent that verifies a finding is never the one that found it, and produces three distinct verdicts (confirmed, needs_validation, rejected) validated against a schema. Cloudflare's test runs reportedly found a single run caught roughly half the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total, since ledgers and findings are additive across runs.
summary.cons: Executing target code (builds, tests, fuzzers) requires an OS-enforced sandbox that disables external networking, uses a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforces resource limits, and restricts writes to scratch paths; without it, leads reportedly stay marked needs_validation rather than being executed. This suggests full use of the skill may be difficult without existing sandbox infrastructure.
summary.fit: Given the sandboxing, Node.js, and parallel-sub-agent model requirements, the skill seems best suited to teams already using capable coding agents and willing to invest in isolated execution environments, rather than serving as a lightweight, drop-in audit tool.

repos.name: milind-soni / OpenMausBot
repos.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use

summary.goal: OpenMausBot is an open-source, Apache 2.0 licensed desktop chat application in which multiple AI agents (via Claude, Codex, and Grok CLIs) run as individual bots in a sidebar, each with its own model, computer, and connected apps. It is presented as an open alternative to products such as Grok Bot, Meta Muse, OpenAI dots, and Manus Cue.
summary.usage: Install globally with `npm install -g openmausbot` and run `openmausbot`, or build from source via `git clone https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot && cd OpenMausBot`, `pnpm install`, then `pnpm dev:server` and `pnpm dev`. The README lists requirements as Node 24+, pnpm, macOS/Windows/Ubuntu 24.04 x64, and at least one of the claude/codex/grok CLIs installed and logged in.
summary.pros: A local harness server on 127.0.0.1 keeps transcripts, keys, and events in `~/.openmausbot` rather than a cloud service. A permission broker surfaces risky actions (shell commands, file edits) as approval cards, and bots can reach over 500 apps through Composio.
summary.cons: The README notes the Windows installer is not yet code-signed, which can trigger SmartScreen warnings, and Ubuntu support remains beta with Wayland host control disabled pending issue #345; CLI-saved API keys are stored as plaintext in config.json rather than encrypted, suggesting security hardening still varies by platform and install path.
summary.fit: This project appears best suited to users who already hold Claude, Codex, or Grok CLI access and want a self-hosted, multi-agent chat interface with local data control, while those expecting a fully managed cloud computer should note Boat, the cloud-computer provider, is a paid service after its trial.

repos.name: pingdotgg / t3code
repos.description: The best way to control Claude Code, Codex and more from any computer or phone

summary.goal: T3 Code is described as an open-source control plane for coding agents, running agents on a local machine and providing one interface for starting threads on desktop and approving steps from a phone. It states compatibility with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any ACP agent.
summary.usage: The desktop app can be downloaded, or installed via package managers like `brew install --cask t3-code` or `winget install T3Tools.T3Code`. The command line tool is installed with `curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh`, after which running `t3` starts the server and opens the web app; `npx t3@latest` can be used to try it without installing.
summary.pros: The README states it does not resell tokens, instead driving agents the user is already signed into, and supports switching models mid-thread across desktop, web, and phone clients from one server. It also describes built-in git support per thread worktree and states the source code is MIT licensed, allowing forking under different branding.
summary.cons: The documentation notes that T3 Code requires at least one agent already installed and signed in separately (for example via `claude auth login` or `codex login`) before it can control it, and states that contribution review capacity is limited, with features needing an approved discussion first.
summary.fit: Based on the README, this tool appears suited for developers who already use one or more supported coding agents and want a unified local-first interface across desktop, web, and mobile, including remote approval workflows via Tailscale or T3 Connect.

repos.name: anthropics / skills
repos.description: Public repository for Agent Skills

summary.goal: This repository provides Anthropic's reference implementation of Skills for Claude — folders containing instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to perform specialized tasks such as document creation, data analysis, or workflow automation.
summary.usage: Skills can be installed in Claude Code as a plugin marketplace via `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`, followed by `/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills` or `/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills`. They are also available directly to paid Claude.ai plans and through the Claude API.
summary.pros: Many skills, including the docx, pdf, pptx, and xlsx document-handling skills that power Claude's document capabilities in production, are released under the Apache 2.0 open-source license, giving developers reusable examples of complex, actively used skills.
summary.cons: The README states these skills are provided for demonstration and educational purposes only, and that actual Claude behavior may differ from what is shown, so users are advised to test skills thoroughly in their own environment before relying on them for critical tasks.
summary.fit: This project appears best suited for developers seeking patterns and inspiration for building their own Claude skills rather than for teams needing a guaranteed production-ready toolset out of the box.

repos.name: thedotmack / claude-mem
repos.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent –  Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More

summary.goal: Claude-Mem gives coding agents persistent memory across sessions. A second agent observes tool activity while the primary agent works and writes compact observations and summaries, so the next session in a project starts with relevant context instead of beginning from zero.
summary.usage: Install with `npx claude-mem install`, which detects supported agents on the machine and sets up each one; it can also be added as a Claude Code plugin via `/plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem` followed by `/plugin install claude-mem`. Memory then builds automatically starting from a project's second session, and `npx claude-mem doctor` helps diagnose setup problems.
summary.pros: It supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and reportedly 11 more agents, with several additional tools (Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code, Warp, Zed) able to search stored memory. Search is described as token-efficient, using a three-step index/timeline/detail workflow, and content wrapped in `<private>` tags is excluded from storage.
summary.cons: Choosing the claude-mem observer provider starts a 30-day free trial that requires entering a payment method at checkout, and memory falls back to the user's Anthropic plan automatically once the trial ends unless they subscribe. The project also requires Node.js 20.19+ (20.x line) or 22.12+, with Bun and uv auto-installed as dependencies.
summary.fit: Released under the Apache License 2.0, Claude-Mem is positioned as straightforward to embed in developer tools, local agents, MCP servers, enterprise systems, robotics stacks, and production agent harnesses; how well it fits a given deployment likely depends on the specific agent and workflow in use.

repos.name: Jakeschincariol / instagram-agent-skill
repos.description: Thirteen Claude skills that run an Instagram account: Reels off 26 scored hook formulas, a viral research skill, a caption linter, and a humanizer. Free, MIT.

summary.goal: instagram-agent-skill provides thirteen Claude skills intended to support running an Instagram account, covering Reel scripting, caption writing, profile scoring, weekly planning, and a humanizer that strips slop vocabulary and invisible characters from drafts. The README states it is free, MIT-licensed, and requires no signup or API key.
summary.usage: Installation is done by pasting the repository URL https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/instagram-agent-skill into Claude, or by running git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/instagram-agent-skill.git followed by copying the skills folders, or via /plugin install. Users are told to first fill in templates/voice.md, then invoke commands such as /ig-reel or local scripts like python3 hookscore.py hooks.txt.
summary.pros: The five Python tools (hookscore.py, beats.py, caption.py, humanize.py, detect.py, swipe.py) reportedly run locally with no dependencies or network calls. An approval gate means nothing is posted automatically, and the caption tool enforces Instagram's current five-hashtag cap effective 18 December 2025. The README also reports an AUC of 0.83 for flagging deliberately weak hooks.
summary.cons: The README states these skills do not post to Instagram directly; real publishing requires a Meta developer app, linked Page, long-lived token, and app review, which the skill cannot provide. It also discloses that the hook scorer's ability to pick winning hooks among good ones is weak, at AUC 0.56, close to a coin flip.
summary.fit: This appears suited to Instagram creators using Claude Code who want drafting, scoring, and planning assistance while retaining manual control over posting. Without Claude Code, the README notes the five Python tools are unavailable, so project-local or plugin installation seems best for full functionality.

repos.name: Ebony-Vinyl / dsh-our-free-model
repos.description: 在 dsh 里装上这个插件即可，无需登录、注册或填 API Key，就能使用包括 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Kimi K3 在内的前沿模型——完全免费，不限量。 All you do is install this plugin in dsh: no login, no sign-up, no API key — the frontier models are just there, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Kimi K3 among them. Completely free, with no usage cap.

summary.goal: dsh-our-free-model is a plugin for the DSH harness that provides access to a free model lane without requiring sign-in, account creation, or an API key. It is installed into DSH as a plugin and targets DSH kernel versions 0.1.5 through 0.1.7-rc.2.
summary.usage: The plugin is installed with the command `dsh plugin --profile web add @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model@2.9.1` (or via a local path for non-npm installs). The repository also documents a separate standalone local service, started with `npm run start:standalone`, that runs independently of DSH and listens on its own port.
summary.pros: The README states the project has zero runtime dependencies, no build step, and an MIT license, and describes the free lane as requiring no account, key, or quota request. It also presents upstream sources (OpenCode's Zen gateway, Kilo AI's public gateway) as disclosed and directly connected rather than routed through third-party relays.
summary.cons: The README warns that a differently-packaged, unscoped `dsh-our-free-model` exists on npm that is not published by this repository and contains modified files, so installing the wrong package name may skip the project's signature verification and in-app upgrade path. The documented free-tier model also lacks a quota dashboard but is rate-limited per session, which the README says can lead to 429 responses under heavy use.
summary.fit: The project is scoped to the DSH plugin ecosystem and documents compatibility with DSH kernel versions 0.1.5 through 0.1.7-rc.2. It also offers a separate standalone local service that does not require installing DSH, though the README notes that standalone installation artifacts and releases have not yet been published.

repos.name: HKUDS / DeepTutor
repos.description: DeepTutor: Lifelong Personalized Tutoring. https://deeptutor.info/.

summary.goal: DeepTutor (HKUDS/DeepTutor) is documented as an agent-native learning workspace that connects tutoring, research, content creation, and practice in a single extensible system, released under the Apache 2.0 license.
summary.usage: The README documents installing with `pip install -U "deeptutor[full]"` followed by `deeptutor init` and `deeptutor start` to launch backend and frontend together, or running `docker run --rm --name deeptutor -p 127.0.0.1:3782:3782 -v deeptutor-data:/app/data ghcr.io/hkuds/deeptutor:latest` to trial the full web app without installing Python or Node.js.
summary.pros: Documented capabilities include a shared runtime across multiple learning modes (Chat, Quiz, Research, Visualize, Solve, Mastery Path, Reading), a connected workspace linking Chat, Books, Reading, Practice, Task Board, and Calendar, grounded knowledge retrieval through multiple RAG engines (LlamaIndex, PageIndex, GraphRAG, LightRAG), consultable agent partners/subagents, and an inspectable three-layer memory system.
summary.cons: Full installation requires Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+ as stated prerequisites, so environments outside that range likely need adjustment before setup succeeds.
summary.fit: Based on its CLI/SDK design for headless operation and NDJSON output described for agent-driven runs, DeepTutor appears best suited for users wanting a self-hosted, extensible tutoring platform that can also be automated or embedded by other agents, rather than a lightweight single-purpose chatbot.

repos.name: pbakaus / impeccable
repos.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.

summary.goal: Impeccable is a design vocabulary and skill set for coding agents, offering steering commands such as `polish` and `bolder`, review commands like `critique` and `audit`, and a slop detector intended to catch common AI-generated design issues before they ship.
summary.usage: From the project root, install Impeccable with `npx impeccable install`, reload the coding tool, then run `/impeccable init`. The detector can also run standalone, e.g. `npx impeccable detect src/`, for CI or terminal use without an agent; further documentation is at https://impeccable.style/docs.
summary.pros: Impeccable's detector applies 62 deterministic rules without requiring an LLM or API key, and the toolkit offers 24 commands grouped into steering, review, finishing, live iteration, and planning. It documents support across many coding agents and integrates with GitHub Actions via SARIF 2.1.0 output.
summary.cons: In Impeccable, live mode edits only a local checkout, and applying copy edits can run an optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with the user's permissions, which the documentation recommends reviewing before use in an unfamiliar repository; installed hooks may also run even when a model's own commands are denied.
summary.fit: Impeccable appears best suited to teams already using one of its many supported coding agents for iterating on existing interfaces, since building entirely new pages is described as a harder mode rather than its primary strength.

repos.name: sherlock-project / sherlock
repos.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks

summary.goal: Sherlock is a command-line tool documented as helping users search for social media accounts tied to a specific username across 400+ social networks.
summary.usage: Installation can be done with `pipx install sherlock-project` (pip or uv are listed as alternatives), via Docker with `docker run -it --rm sherlock/sherlock`, or `dnf install sherlock-project`. To search, run `sherlock user123` for one username or `sherlock user1 user2 user3` for several; found accounts are saved to text files, and `sherlock --help` lists all available flags.
summary.pros: The README lists multiple installation routes (pipx/pip/uv, Docker, dnf), export options in CSV and XLSX formats, proxy support via `--proxy`, and flags for filtering specific sites, adjusting timeouts, and controlling output verbosity.
summary.cons: The documentation notes that third-party packages for ParrotOS and Ubuntu 24.04 are currently reported as broken, and that community-maintained packages for Debian, Ubuntu, Homebrew, Kali, and BlackArch are not directly supported or maintained by the Sherlock Project itself.
summary.fit: Based on the documented features, this tool may be best suited for OSINT-style username enumeration on systems with Python/pipx or Docker available; it is currently at version 0.16.0 and distributed under the MIT license.

repos.name: AgriciDaniel / claude-seo
repos.description: Universal SEO skill for Claude Code. 26 sub-skills + 19 sub-agents covering technical SEO, E-E-A-T, schema, GEO/AEO, agent readiness (Lighthouse Agentic Browsing, WebMCP, llms.txt), backlinks, local SEO, e-commerce, international SEO, Google APIs, and PDF/Excel reporting. 9 optional extensions for live SEO data.

summary.goal: Claude SEO is a free, open-source SEO audit plugin for Claude Code. It runs a full website audit in 10 to 15 minutes and returns a prioritized action plan covering technical SEO, content quality (E-E-A-T), Schema.org structured data, AI search (GEO), and local/e-commerce SEO.
summary.usage: Inside Claude Code 1.0.33 or newer, install with `/plugin marketplace add AgriciDaniel/claude-seo` followed by `/plugin install claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo`, then run `/seo setup` to prepare the runtime. Start an audit with `/seo audit <url>`.
summary.pros: Claude SEO is MIT licensed with no per-site pricing, no usage limits, and no tracking, and it works without API keys out of the box. It uses 29 sub-skills and 20 specialist agents, with up to 17 agents auditing a site in parallel.
summary.cons: Without connecting Google API keys, Core Web Vitals are reported as lab estimates and indexing status is inferred rather than directly measured, and pages that load content only after scrolling or clicking can produce noisy results. A full `/seo audit` also uses Opus for five agents, consuming more of a Claude plan than a single-page check.
summary.fit: According to the documentation, it targets SEO agencies wanting frequent client audits with change monitoring, in-house SEO teams wanting a recurring second check including AI search, and freelance consultants wanting a quick audit and score before writing a proposal.

repos.name: heygen-com / hyperframes
repos.description: Open-source AI video editor: edit your own footage, or create and remake any video with Claude Code, Codex or the free Studio app. Write HTML, render MP4. By HeyGen.

summary.goal: HyperFrames is HeyGen's open-source (Apache 2.0) AI video editor and rendering framework that turns HTML, CSS, JavaScript, media and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. It serves both people, via the HyperFrames Studio app, and coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, without requiring React.
summary.usage: Three ways to use it: download the HyperFrames Studio app (free plan); install coding-agent skills with `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`; or use the CLI directly — `npx hyperframes init my-video`, then `npx hyperframes preview` and `npx hyperframes render` to produce an MP4 file.
summary.pros: Licensed under Apache 2.0, HyperFrames has no per-render fees or commercial-use thresholds. It is HTML-native with no build step, renders deterministically (same input, same output) for CI and regression testing, and supports animation libraries such as GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js and WAAPI.
summary.cons: Local CLI rendering requires Node.js 22 or later plus FFmpeg installed beforehand. The optional Studio Pro plan costs $25 a month for added models and credits. Community-maintained skills are explicitly flagged for review before use, suggesting their quality and safety may vary.
summary.fit: HyperFrames may suit teams or agents more comfortable authoring video as plain HTML/CSS/JS than as React components, since its comparison with Remotion notes Remotion requires a bundler while HyperFrames needs no build step — a difference that could favor automated, agent-driven video pipelines over React-centric workflows.

repos.name: vercel-labs / agent-browser
repos.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents

summary.goal: agent-browser is presented as a native Rust command-line tool that gives AI agents a browser they can drive one command at a time, for browser automation such as opening pages, reading them as an accessibility tree, and acting on elements from the shell.
summary.usage: Install with `npm install -g agent-browser`, then run `agent-browser install` once to download Chrome for Testing. A typical session uses `agent-browser open example.com`, `agent-browser snapshot -i` to list interactive elements with refs, `agent-browser click @e1` to act on a ref, `agent-browser get url` to check the result, and `agent-browser close` to end the session.
summary.pros: The browser stays open between commands, so each step is a single short shell call. The `snapshot` command returns compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element, letting an agent act and then re-check the page. The project also documents multiple browser engines and cloud providers alongside the default Chrome for Testing, and ships native binaries for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
summary.cons: Refs only describe the page at the moment of the snapshot, so a new snapshot is required after navigation or a DOM change before reusing a ref. A click reports failure rather than succeeding when its target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element. By default the background daemon also closes the headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, which suggests long-idle workflows may need session persistence configured separately.
summary.fit: Given its one-command-at-a-time design and MCP server support (`agent-browser mcp`), it appears aimed at AI agent harnesses and MCP clients needing scriptable browser control, and is also documented for use within Vercel Sandbox and eve agents.
